Z₁ = 3 + j4 Ω and Z₂ = 5 − j2 Ω are in series. Z_eq is

Rule: series impedances add, real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts.
Apply: (3 + 5) + j(4 − 2) = 8 + j2 Ω.
Check: 8 + j6 adds the imaginary parts as if both were positive, 2 + j6 subtracts the real parts, 15 − j8 is a product.
Two equal impedances of 10∠30° Ω are in parallel. Z_eq is

Rule: two equal impedances in parallel give half of one, and the angle does not change.
Apply: 10∠30° / 2 = 5∠30° Ω.
Check: 20∠30° is the series value, 5∠60° changes the angle, 10∠15° changes both.
j10 Ω and −j10 Ω are in series. The total impedance is

Rule: an inductor and a capacitor have opposite signs.
Apply: j10 + (−j10) = 0 Ω.
Check: j20 and −j20 add equal signs, 10 Ω is only a magnitude.
R = 4 Ω is in parallel with Z = j4 Ω. The magnitude of Z_eq is

Rule: Z_eq = Z₁ Z₂ / (Z₁ + Z₂).
Apply: (4)(j4) / (4 + j4) = j16 / (4 + j4) = 2 + j2 Ω, so |Z_eq| = 2.83 Ω.
Check: 8 Ω is the sum of the magnitudes, 5.66 Ω doubles the answer, 4 Ω is just R.
A series circuit has E = 50∠0° V, Z₁ = 6 Ω and Z₂ = j8 Ω. The voltage across Z₂ is

Rule: voltage divider: V₂ = E Z₂ / (Z₁ + Z₂).
Apply: |Z_T| = 10 Ω at 53.13°, so V₂ = 50 × (8∠90°) / (10∠53.13°) = 40∠36.87° V.
Check: 30∠−53.13° is the voltage across Z₁, the angle −53.13° forgets the 90° of Z₂, and 50 V is the whole source.
Which rule gives the current I₁ in Z₁ when Z₁ and Z₂ are in parallel and the total current is I_T?

Rule: the current divider puts the other impedance on top.
Apply: I₁ = I_T Z₂ / (Z₁ + Z₂).
Check: putting Z₁ on top gives I₂, and the other two forms are not a divider.
Z₁ = 2 Ω and Z₂ = j3 Ω are in series on 10∠0° V. The magnitude of the current is

Rule: I = E / Z with Z = Z₁ + Z₂.
Apply: Z = 2 + j3 Ω, |Z| = 3.61 Ω, and I = 10 / 3.61 = 2.77 A.
Check: 2 A, 3.33 A and 5 A use only one part of the impedance.
Z = 6 + j8 Ω. The impedance angle is

Rule: φ = tan⁻¹(X / R).
Apply: tan⁻¹(8 / 6) = 53.13°.
Check: 36.87° is tan⁻¹(6 / 8), −53.13° belongs to a capacitive load, 8° is just the reactance.
In the impedance triangle, the hypotenuse is

Rule: R and X are the two sides at the right angle.
Apply: |Z|² = R² + X², so |Z| is the hypotenuse.
Check: R and X are the sides and φ is an angle.
R = 5 Ω and X_L = 12 Ω are in series. The magnitude |Z| is

Rule: |Z| = √(R² + X²).
Apply: √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 Ω.
Check: 17 Ω adds the sides, 7 Ω subtracts them, 60 Ω multiplies them.
A circuit has Z = 10∠−30° Ω. It is

Rule: a negative angle means that the net reactance X is negative.
Apply: φ = −30° < 0, so X_C is larger than X_L: the circuit is capacitive.
Check: inductive needs φ > 0, purely resistive needs φ = 0 and resonance means X = 0.
Z = 10∠60° Ω. The resistance R is

Rule: R = |Z| cos φ.
Apply: 10 × cos 60° = 5 Ω.
Check: 8.66 Ω is |Z| sin φ (the reactance), 10 Ω is |Z|, 17.3 Ω is |Z| tan φ.
R = 3 Ω and X_L = 4 Ω are in series. The power factor is

Rule: PF = cos φ = R / |Z|.
Apply: |Z| = 5 Ω, so PF = 3 / 5 = 0.6, and X_L > 0 means lagging.
Check: 0.8 is sin φ, leading needs a capacitive load, 1 needs X = 0.
In a series RLC circuit X_L = X_C. The impedance angle φ is

Rule: X = X_L − X_C.
Apply: X = 0, so Z = R and φ = 0°.
Check: ±90° belongs to a pure L or C, 45° needs X = R.
